abstract: Transport of lipids within cells is crucial for cellular functions and is facilitated by lipid transport proteins, like the Saccharomyces cerevisiae oxysterol-binding homologue (Osh) proteins. Among these, Osh4 is of particular interest, due to its role in lipid trafficking at the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and trans-Golgi network (TGN). Here, we elucidate the membrane-binding mechanism of the amphipathic lipid packing sensor (ALPS)-like motif of Osh4 using circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) integrated with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Our findings show environment-dependent structural changes of the ALPS peptide, including a preference for -helical structure in the presence of phospholipid membranes which is modestly enhanced in the presence of anionic lipids. Fluorescence spectroscopy and MD simulation results corroborate the ALPS peptide's interaction with model membranes and reveal slightly enhanced binding to membranes containing anionic lipids. Moreover, XRD demonstrated the peptide influences membrane structure, with thinning observed upon peptide incorporation. We determined the binding affinity of the ALPS peptide to model membranes using ITC, which supports enthalpy-driven contributions between anionic lipids and the lysine in the ALPS peptide and an entropic contribution from serine and threonine residues desolvating into the membrane. Comparison with computational estimates using potential of mean force calculations suggests current force fields overestimate binding energy. Overall, our results support that the ALPS-like motif will preferentially bind to the TGN cytosolic leaflet, which contains a higher concentration of anionic lipids compared to the ER, providing insight into lipid transport by Osh4.
